info.bio: Stereophonics son un grupo de Cwmaman, Gales formado en 1992 y llamada en sus comienzos Tragic Love Company, inspirándose en los nombres de sus grupos favoritos Tragically Hip, Mother Love Bone y Bad Company. Comenzaron como banda juvenil y más tarde, inspirados en un gramófono de la abuela de Stuart, cambiaron su nombre al actual. Proceden de Cwmaman, en el sur de Gales. Tras cambiar su nombre fueron una de las primeras bandas en firmar por la discográfica de Richard Branson V2 en Agosto de 1996.

scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: "Stereophonics" Name Origin
podcast.body: The final band name, Stereophonics, was taken from the name of a record player manufacturer. "Finally, the name Stereophonics. That was caught from the name of a record player manufacturer."

podcast.body: The name "Trajik Love Company" was an amalgamation of the band's three favorite groups: The Tragically Hip, Mother Love Bone, and Bad Company. podcast.title: Continued Success and Local Connection
podcast.body: The band has achieved success with multiple singles and albums, enabling them to make a "very nice living" by touring the world while still maintaining homes in their tiny, dead-end mining town in South Wales. "Singles turned into an album and one album became two and three and more. And now Stereophonics are making a very nice living by touring the world while still owning homes in the tiny dead-end mining town in South Wales, which as far as I can tell, has a population holding at about 1000."

podcast.title: Cwmaman, South Wales Origins - Population ~1,000
podcast.body: Stereophonics originated from Cwmaman, a small village in South Wales with a population estimated at about 1,000. It is located at the end of a dead-end road, meaning the only road in is also the only road out, fostering a close-knit community. "But as for the smallest town the Gave birth to an internationally-known band, we have to go to Wales, in a town that has way too many consonants and way too few vowels. It's, quote, quote, quote, a man. C-W-M-A-M-A, I don't know. My apologies to the Welsh people for my horrible pronunciation. The village is at the end of a dead end road in South Wales. The only road in is the only road out. In other words, no one can just drive through quimmon men. This makes for a very close-knit place."

podcast.title: Early Band Formation Idea
podcast.body: Around the age of ten, Kelly Jones, Stuart Cable, and Richard Jones met in a park and began discussing the idea of forming a band. "When there were all about ten years old, all three guys been in the park and started talking about forming a band."

podcast.title: Evolution of Band Names
podcast.body: Over the years, the band went through several names, starting with Zephyr's, then Trajik Love Company, before settling on Stereophonics. "Over the years, they had several. The first was Zephyr's, then it was Trajik Love Company, which is actually an interesting story."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Former Coal Mining Town
podcast.body: Cwmaman is a former coal mining town where the mine has been shut for years. Despite the closure, many residents chose to stay, contributing to the town's unique character. "It's also a former coal mining town. The mine has been shut for years, but even so a lot of people decided to stay on."

podcast.title: Shared Birthplace and Childhood Proximity
podcast.body: All three founding members of Stereophonics were born in the same nearby hospital. Kelly Jones lived just eight doors away from drummer Stuart Cable and his mother, Mabel Cable. Bass player Richard Jones lived across the street from the local football pitch. "All three founding members of Stereophonics were born in the same nearby hospital. Kelly Jones, the leader of the band, lived just eight doors away from drummer Stuart Cable and his mother, Mabel. That's right her name is Mabel Cable. Meanwhile Richard Jones, the bass player, lived in the house across the street from the football pitch."

podcast.body: After a series of out-of-town gigs supporting bigger bands, Stereophonics became one of the first acts signed to Richard Branson's new V2 label. "After a series of out of town gigs supporting bigger bands, they became one of the first sunnings to Richard Branson's new V2 label."

podcast.title: Stuart Cable's Rush Fandom
podcast.body: Drummer Stuart Cable was noted as being a "huge, huge Rush fan," highlighting an interesting Canadian music influence on the band from a small Welsh town.
